user.title: Add Truma iNet X
user.description: Select the Truma panel to add.

data_description.address: The Truma panel to pair with. Only panels currently advertising within range of Home Assistant's Bluetooth, whether that is an ESP32 proxy or a local adapter, are listed.

confirm.description: Do you want to add the Truma panel {name}?

pair.title: Pair with the Truma panel
pair.description:
Put the panel {name} into add-device mode (in the Truma InetX app, or on the panel itself), then select **Submit** once. Pairing can take up to a minute.

**If pairing fails, work through these in order:**

1. **Clear the panel's saved Bluetooth device list.** It stores only about four devices and silently rejects new bonds once full. Put the panel back into add-device mode and try again.
2. **If clearing the list did not help, power-cycle the panel and start over** — switch it off, back on, put it into add-device mode again, and repeat this step. A power-cycle drops stale connections that hold a slot and makes the panel advertise a fresh Bluetooth address, which pairs cleanly. This resolves most stubborn cases.

Always re-enter add-device mode before each attempt: the panel only accepts a bond while its pairing screen is up.

error.pairing_failed: Could not pair with the panel. Put it back into add-device mode and try again. If that fails, clear its saved Bluetooth device list (it holds only about four devices); if clearing the list does not help either, power-cycle the panel, put it into add-device mode again and start over.

no_route.title: Nothing can connect to the Truma panel
no_route.description:
Home Assistant can hear the Truma panel advertising, but none of the Bluetooth adapters or proxies it has can connect to it.

The panel uses a rotating Bluetooth private address, and it only answers a connect that puts its *current* address on air. Whether that happens depends on the host:

- A Linux kernel below 6.19 does it in software, so a plain local adapter works.
- From 6.19 onwards the kernel sends the panel's identity address instead, which the panel does not answer. A local adapter then only works if its controller supports LL Privacy and BlueZ has programmed the panel's key into the resolving list, which it currently does not do for this kind of bond. A kernel fix is posted upstream and not yet merged.
- An ESPHome Bluetooth proxy's controller does it itself, on any host.

Check that the panel is in range of whichever of these you have, and that nothing else is holding a connection to it. Note that a bond lives on the adapter it was made with: if the adapter or proxy that paired the panel is no longer there, the panel has to be paired again.

Home Assistant chooses which adapter or proxy to connect through by itself; this integration does not pin the panel to one.

data_description.poll_interval_seconds: 0 keeps the connection open, so changes show up instantly. A non-zero value connects, takes a reading and disconnects again -- slower, but it frees the adapter's connection slot between readings, which matters when other Bluetooth devices share the same adapter.
